newsitem.title: USA: Yahoo! tops Wall Street Q2 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Yahoo! tops Wall Street Q2 estimates.

text.p: Yahoo! Inc. Wednesday reported a better-than-expected second quarter profit, helped by growth in traffic on its Internet navigation site on the World Wide Web.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based company reported a profit of $610,000, or 2 cents a share, compared with a loss of $1.4 million, or 5 cents a share in the year earlier period. Revenues more than quadrupled to $13.5 million from $3.3 million.
It was the company's third straight quarter of profits and compared with Wall Street expectations of a 1-cent-a-share loss.
Yahoo said traffic on its site grew by more than 26 percent to an average 38 million page views a day during the month of June, compared with more than 30 million in March.
Yahoo also said it remained the No. 1 search and navigation site on the Internet for the sixth consecutive quarter.
The company's report was issued after the close of the market, but anticipation of solid results helped drive the stock $4.25 higher to $44 on Nasdaq.
Hambrecht & Quist analyst Paul Noglows said revenues were $1 million above his estimates and more than $2 million above Wall Street's consensus estimates of $11.3 million.
"They showed good traffic numbers," he said.

Yahoo's average cost per thousand ad impressions, or CPM, a metric used in Internet advertising, remain in the $20 to $25 range, Yahoo Chief Executive Officer Tim Koogle said, adding that the company continues to have "a ton of headroom" into which to sell additional ads.
Yahoo had exceeded 1 million registered users in its chat services, Koogle said.

Koogle said a deal with Netscape Communications Corp. for Yahoo to provide search-and-navigation services in 12 countries in Europe and Asia also trims Yahoo!'s minimum payment as part of its earlier Netscape Guide by Yahoo! deal to $4.7 million from $10 million for the first year.
